newsitem.title: USA: GTECH says judge recommend Fla. award reevaluation.
newsitem.headline: GTECH says judge recommend Fla. award reevaluation.

text.p: GTECH Corp on Wednesday said an Administrative Law Judge of the State of Florida has recommended that the Florida State Lottery reevaluate its previously announced award for the lottery system and services to Automated Wagering International Inc.
Automated Wagering is a unit of Video Lottery Technologies Inc.

GTECH said Judge Charles Adams, of the Division of Administrative Hearings, cited the Lottery evaluation committee in numerous instances for taking action that were erroneous, contrary to competition and arbitrary.
In November, Florida awarded a five year contract to Automated Wagering, valued at about $27.7 million annually, based on prior year lottery sales.
A Video Lottery spokeswoman was not immediately available to comment on the news.
GTech said the Judge's decision is not binding, but added the Florida Lottery Secretary must act on the judge's recommendations by June 4, 1997.

GTech said the judge found Lottery evaluators inappropriately favored AWI as the incumbent vendor, improperly and inappropriately scored GTech on technical grounds and misled and misinformed GTech with respect to the manner in which pricing proposals would be evaluated.
The judge recommended that Florida's Lottery Secretary enter a final order that would reconvene the evaluation committee and require the committee to rescore portions of the proposal.
